title: Coldstart allocator backpressure and prefix-cache shadowing causing intermittent Private/Gated OOMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers running Private and Dedicated deployments reported intermittent full-GPU OOMs during coldstart bursts and deployment scaling. The failure pattern diverges from ordinary KV-cache leakage: memory consumption grows sharply during 'warmup churn' when many short-lived sessions initialize model KV caches concurrently. Investigations point to a combination of allocator backpressure, prefix-cache shadowing (duplicate KV entries created in transient session state), and delayed async evictions under load.

Scope:
- Affects Private (VPC) nodes with mixed-priority tenant scheduling and Dedicated pools under fast autoscale-in/out.
- Manifests as 1) immediate OOMs within first 20–90s of heavy request bursts, 2) long tail memory retention preventing recovery until manual evict or restart.

Hypothesis and root causes considered:
- Allocator fragmentation + small-slab saturation when many short-lived tensor arenas are allocated concurrently (coldstart).
- Prefix/KV shadowing: session initialization duplicates small KV fragments before global dedupe completes, causing transient double-allocated metadata and pointers.
- Async evict backlog: eviction thread pool falls behind under bursty traffic, queueing tombstone work that keeps memory pinned.
- Cross-node scheduling: tenants shifted between nodes during autoscale cause double-writes to ephemeral caches and delayed tombstone reconciliation.

Impact:
Multiple customers (5 known escalations) experienced production outages or degraded latency. One large customer opened a Sev2 on 2026-02-21 for a private deployment used for regulated workloads.
updates: 2026-02-21: Initial customer report received (Sev2). Logged heap profiles and kernel traces; reproduced OOM locally with stress harness using 300 concurrent short-lived sessions.
2026-02-22: Short-term mitigation deployed: reduce concurrent session warmup throttling on Private nodes and temporarily increase per-node swap margin to avoid immediate OOM during peak bursts.

2026-02-24: Heap profile analysis indicates a consistent 18–27% of GPU memory held by duplicate small KV metadata allocations during the first 60s of load. Allocator slab utilization shows rapid growth in smallest size-classes.

2026-02-27: Engineering decision: implement two-stage patch set — (A) runtime: conservative allocator pre-warming for coldstart and small-slab pooling; (B) kvcache: prefix dedupe gate to prevent transient double-insert, plus faster tombstone drain strategy.

2026-03-02: Prototype allocator pre-warm landed in branch 'alloc-prewarm-ENG701234' (GH PR #14892). Perf tests show median coldstart tail latency increase ~4% but reduces OOM rate to zero in repro harness.
2026-03-04: Design review with Infra and SRE: trade-off accepted — slight coldstart latency vs elimination of high-severity OOMs. PM approved rollout to canary clusters.

2026-03-06: Prefix dedupe gate implementation (kvcache) merged (GH PR #14931). Unit tests added. Discovered a race when dedupe gating interacts with session handoff; added a per-session sequence token to resolve ordering.
2026-03-08: Canary rollout to 3 Private clusters. Observed 0 customer-facing OOMs in canaries over 48h, eviction backlog reduced by 72% in internal dashboards.

2026-03-09: Post-rollout bug: one Dedicated pool exhibited increased memory pressure after long-tail sessions; root cause traced to dedupe gate not cleaning up cancelled warmups. Hotfix PR #14978 prepared.
2026-03-10: Hotfix merged and rolled to canaries; monitoring shows memory pressure back within baseline. Preparing full production rollout and follow-up monitoring run for 7 days before marking Done.
action_items: Roll out runtime-1.23 candidate with alloc-prewarm and kvcache dedupe to all Private clusters (SRE window: 2026-03-12).
Add robust metrics for prefix-shadow count and per-session warmup cancellation rate (owner: Observability).
Follow-up: design a permanent asynchronous tombstone prioritizer to avoid backlog under autoscale-in/out (owner: Runtime).
Postmortem write-up and customer communications (owner: Customer Success + PM).
resolution_plan: 1) Full production rollout after 7-day canary stabilization window; 2) Monitor OOM/evict backlog and revert knobs if regressions observed; 3) Schedule deeper allocator refactor (Q2) to reduce small-slab fragmentation long-term.
